newTerms.spirit-fusion series: serie de fusión con el Espíritu

forcedChoices.choice: «que, según lo que elija ese mortal, puede consumar»
forcedChoices.reason: The relative «que» keeps open whether the Adjuster or the essence (or the mind) consummates the union, as the English «which» does.

forcedChoices.choice: «edad del buen juicio» for «age of discretion»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish «discreción» reads as tact or reserve; «buen juicio» carries the mature judgment that the English means.
Spanish «orden» in the sense of a class or rank of beings is masculine; the feminine «la orden» is kept only for «la orden de Miguel» (an order as a body, 107:3.9).

forcedChoices.choice: «para que termine la soledad de ellos»
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish «su» would be ambiguous between the readers and the Adjusters; the English «their loneliness» is the Adjusters' loneliness.

forcedChoices.choice: «adaptan, modifican y sustituyen» without a reflexive «se»
forcedChoices.reason: The English verbs have no object; the plain transitive form without an object keeps both readings (they adapt themselves, or they adapt their plans).
Both verbs share the object, as in English, so the reading of «supremacizes» as transitive or intransitive stays open.
